title: Feelings
source: User-provided workbook photo, manually transcribed; Word File German translations suggested separately

entries.description: Very cross; mad
Not able to do anything to change a situation
Feeling good about something you or others did well
A bit cross because someone bothers you
Sad because someone was unkind to you
Very upset because something bad happened suddenly
Upset because you can't do or get what you want
Feeling that people don't get what you mean
Feeling this when something unexpected happens

entries.example: To advance the agenda, many governments are taking action.
entries.description: To move something forward

entries.example: The town's fast development has brought many new businesses to the area.
entries.description: The process of growing or changing

entries.example: The company reported a gain this year.
entries.description: An increase; profit

entries.example: Gender equality means treating men and women equally.
entries.description: When men and women have the same rights

entries.example: The team worked together to solve the issue.
entries.description: A problem or important topic

entries.example: The living conditions in the new apartment are comfortable and modern.
entries.description: The situation in which people live, e.g. their home

entries.example: We need to stop pollution and save the environment.
entries.description: Dirty air, water or soil

entries.example: The team made progress on the project after the brainstorming session.
entries.description: Moving forward and getting better

entries.example: The computer lab is an essential resource for students.
entries.description: Something useful that you can use, e.g. money or materials

entries.example: Using solar panels is a sustainable way to produce electricity.
entries.description: Good for the environment in the long term

entries.example: He made a living by working as a cook.
entries.description: To earn enough money to live

entries.example: She got a pay rise for her good work.
entries.description: When your boss gives you more money

entries.example: Coffee beans are dried and then roasted.
entries.description: To cook something in an oven or over a fire

entries.example: Only the best beans are selected.
entries.description: To choose

entries.example: The supermarket has a wide range of goods.
entries.description: Things that are made to be sold

entries.example: Regular exercise is very important for our well-being.
entries.description: Feeling healthy and happy

entries.example: The farmer's goat ate the grass from the field.
entries.description: A farm animal with horns that gives milk

entries.example: The man who married my sister is my brother-in-law.
entries.description: Your sister's husband

entries.example: He defeated the champion in three sets.
entries.description: To win against someone

entries.example: Our dream is that all the peoples of the world should live in harmony.
entries.description: Living together in peace

entries.example: Human beings are the people on this planet Earth.
entries.description: A person

entries.example: He was horrible. He said some hurtful things to me.
entries.description: Unkind; making you feel sad

entries.example: Their ignorance makes them do stupid things.
entries.description: Not knowing about something

entries.example: I want to overcome my fear of flying.
entries.description: To deal with a problem or fear successfully

entries.example: Martin Luther King Jr. led the anti-racism movement for civil rights in America.
entries.description: Unfair treatment of people because of their skin colour

entries.example: He made racist comments about people of colour.
entries.description: Describing a person or a remark that is unfair to people of another skin colour

entries.example: She got a lot of recognition for her work.
entries.description: Praise for something you have done

entries.example: For 200 years, Africans were sold into slavery in America.
entries.description: When people are owned by others and must work for free

entries.example: Your son-in-law is your daughter's husband.
entries.description: Your daughter's husband

entries.example: She claims she saw an alien in her garden last night.
entries.description: To say that something is true

entries.example: Even though it was an accident, he felt guilty about breaking the vase.
entries.description: Feeling bad because you did something wrong

entries.example: When I get better, I'll come round to your place for a visit.
entries.description: To visit someone at their home
